import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_43/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_43/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Both sources have the same schema and contain all needed columns for the target.
# We perform UNION (concatenation) of the two dataframes.

# Select only the columns needed for the target, in the target order:
target_columns = ['artist_name', 'speechiness', 'instrumentalness', 'danceability', 'energy', 'acousticness']

df0_sel = df0[target_columns]
df1_sel = df1[target_columns]

# Concatenate the two dataframes (union)
df_union = pd.concat([df0_sel, df1_sel], ignore_index=True)

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema:
# artist_name: string
df_union['artist_name'] = df_union['artist_name'].astype(str)
# speechiness, instrumentalness, danceability, energy, acousticness: float
float_cols = ['speechiness', 'instrumentalness', 'danceability', 'energy', 'acousticness']
df_union[float_cols] = df_union[float_cols].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_43/target_multisource.csv"
df_union.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_43/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_43/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on artist_name (primary key)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="artist_name", suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# Select and rename columns to match target schema by averaging the two sources' values
# Columns to aggregate: speechiness, instrumentalness, danceability, energy, acousticness
# artist_name is the key and grouping column

# Prepare a DataFrame with artist_name and mean of each attribute from both sources
agg_df = joined.groupby("artist_name").agg({
    'speechiness_0': 'mean',
    'speechiness_1': 'mean',
    'instrumentalness_0': 'mean',
    'instrumentalness_1': 'mean',
    'danceability_0': 'mean',
    'danceability_1': 'mean',
    'energy_0': 'mean',
    'energy_1': 'mean',
    'acousticness_0': 'mean',
    'acousticness_1': 'mean'
}).reset_index()

# Compute mean of each pair of columns from the two sources
agg_df['speechiness'] = agg_df[['speechiness_0', 'speechiness_1']].mean(axis=1)
agg_df['instrumentalness'] = agg_df[['instrumentalness_0', 'instrumentalness_1']].mean(axis=1)
agg_df['danceability'] = agg_df[['danceability_0', 'danceability_1']].mean(axis=1)
agg_df['energy'] = agg_df[['energy_0', 'energy_1']].mean(axis=1)
agg_df['acousticness'] = agg_df[['acousticness_0', 'acousticness_1']].mean(axis=1)

# Select only the target columns in correct order
result = agg_df[['artist_name', 'speechiness', 'instrumentalness', 'danceability', 'energy', 'acousticness']]

# Write to target CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_43/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
